questions.question: Which Central agency issues currency notes on behalf of Central Government?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Reserve Bank of India**__. 

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India__ (RBI) **is India's highest monetary institution.
 
• RBI was** __established in 1935__ by the RBI Act 1934**.
 
• RBI- Foreign Reserve, bank of banks, acts as banker and debt controller of the Government of India.
 
• **It is also responsible for printing notes and managing the supply of money in the Indian economy**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India has the monopoly of printing the currency in the country.
 
• It has the right to issue **all types of notes** except** one rupee note.**

**Note-**

 
• Currency notes and coins of** one rupee and lower denominations are issued by the Ministry of Finance**.
 
• Under the** Coinage Act, 1906,** the Government of India has the sole right to mint coins.
 
• According to** Section 24(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, **RBI is not entitled to issue banknote of denomination of value of one rupee.
 
• The currency note of** one rupee is issued by the Ministry of Finance **and **signed by the Finance Secretary of India**.

questions.question: What is a government budget?

options.text: A report on the economic growth of a country.
A plan for managing personal finances.
A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.
A document outlining foreign policy goals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A government budget is a **financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period**, usually a fiscal year.
 
• The budget outlines the government's financial plans, including how it intends to allocate resources to various sectors such as defense, education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
 
• It serves as a tool for economic policy, allowing the government to manage the economy by controlling public spending and taxation.
 
• The budget also includes proposals for new taxes or changes to existing tax rates, as well as plans for borrowing and debt management.
 
• It reflects the government's priorities and is a key document for ensuring transparency and accountability in public finance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The government budget is typically presented annually in the parliament or legislative assembly by the finance minister.
 
• It is subject to debate and approval by the legislative body before being implemented.
 
• The budget process involves several stages, including proposal, review, approval, implementation, and evaluation.
 
• Effective budgeting is crucial for maintaining fiscal discipline and achieving sustainable economic growth.
 
• Governments around the world use budgets to plan for both short-term and long-term financial goals.

questions.question: GDP is an indicator of a country’s economy. What does ‘D’ in GDP stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Domestic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• GDP stands for** Gross Domestic Product,** which is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a **specific time period.**
 
• The 'D' in GDP refers to the** domestic aspect** of the country's economy, meaning that only **goods and services **produced within the country's borders are included in the calculation.
 
• The **rate of GDP growth** is a crucial gauge of a **nation's economic health.**
 
• A **nation's level of consumption, investment, government spending on goods and services,** and the **profit margin between exports and imports** can all be included in an equation to represent GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development **is a term used to describe the** growth and progress** of a country's economy over time.
 
• **Dividend** refers to the payment made to **shareholders of a company. **
 
• **Deficit** refers to a situation where a** country's expenses exceed** its revenue.

questions.question: What is the full form of GDP?
questions.solution:
• **Gross Domestic Product** is a monetary measure of the market value of all the final goods and services produced in a period of time.
 
• GDP is the sum of the market values, or prices, of all final goods and services produced in an economy during a period of time.

questions.question: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bilateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A bilateral trade agreement is a pact between two parties, countries, or regions that outlines the terms and conditions for trade between them.**

 
 
• In it, both parties agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to promote trade and investment.
 
• It can help to increase economic growth, create job opportunities, and improve the standard of living in both countries.
 
• **India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) are examples of bilateral agreements.**
 
 
 
• Trade Agreements** **are treaties in which a country promises to engage in fewer trade protections with another country (or countries) to engage in more trade.
 
 
• It can be between two countries or between many countries.
 
• Important terms of trade between them include tariffs, quotas, restrictions on imports and exports, and provisions such as trade facilitation, intellectual property rights, and investment protection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A multilateral trade agreement involves three or more countries or regions that agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers.
 
 
• **The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), among the 15 members, is an example.**
 
• **The World Trade Organization (WTO) is another example of a multilateral trade agreement.**
 
 
 
• A tripartite trade agreement involves three parties, usually countries or regions, that agree to promote trade and investment between them.
 
 
• The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is an example of a tripartite trade agreement between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
 
 
 
• **A unilateral trade agreement is a decision made by one country or region to reduce or eliminate trade barriers without the agreement of another party.**
 
 
• This is usually a preferential arrangement that a developed country makes for imports from developing countries.
 
• The United States has unilateral trade policies under the Generalized System of Preferences.

questions.question: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?

options.text: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
Lack of vitamins in regular diet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Excessive intake of high calorie foods**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excessive intake of high calorie foods** is a primary reason for obesity, especially in rapidly urbanizing areas.
 
• Urbanization often leads to lifestyle changes that include increased consumption of fast food, sugary beverages, and other high-calorie, low-nutrient foods.
 
• This dietary shift, combined with reduced physical activity, contributes significantly to weight gain and obesity.
 
• Obesity is associated with various health issues such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and hypertension.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Obesity is defined as having a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher.
 
• Urban environments often provide less opportunity for physical activity due to sedentary jobs and limited access to recreational areas.
 
• Public health initiatives aimed at reducing obesity often focus on promoting healthier eating habits and increasing physical activity.
 
• Other factors contributing to obesity include genetics, metabolism, behavior, and culture.
 
• Addressing obesity requires a multifaceted approach including education, policy changes, and community support.

questions.question: In which type of economy there is neither exports nor imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Closed.**__

 
• An economy having no economic relationship with other countries is called a **closed economy.**

 
 
• **There is neither exports nor imports in a closed economy.**
 
• Goods are produced and consumed by the same households within a closed economy.
 
• The hunter-gatherer societies are the best examples of a closed economy.
 
• A closed economy should be **entirely self-sufficient.**
 
• There are no nations that have economies that are completely closed in reality.
 
 
 
• An economy that has economic relations with other countries of the world is called an **open economy.**
 
 
• There should be exports and imports in an open economy.
 
• Exporting is the process of selling goods or services to a foreign country.
 
• Importing is the process of buying goods or services from a foreign country.
 
 
 
• The economy that left to the free market, and part of it is managed by the government called a **mixed economy.**
 
 
• Both privately owned businesses and governments play important roles in a mixed economy.
 
 
 
• The interconnected worldwide economic activities that take place between multiple countries is called a **global economy.**

questions.question: What is a fiscal year?

questions.question: National defence, roads, government administration are examples of which types of goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public goods**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Public goods** are those that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous. 

 
 
• This means that:

 
 
• **Non-excludable**: Once provided, no one can be excluded from using them.
 
• **Non-rivalrous**: One person’s use of the good does not reduce its availability for others.
 
 
 
 
 
• Public goods like **national defence**, **roads**, and **government administration** are essential services that benefit the entire population

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complementary Goods**:

 
 
• These are **goods that are used together, where the use of one increases the demand for the other (e.g., cars and petrol).**
 
• **Example**: Cars and petrol, printers and ink cartridges, or smartphones and apps.
 
• A rise in the price of one complementary good (e.g., petrol) may decrease the demand for the other (e.g., cars).
 
 
 
• **Private Goods**:
 
 
• Private goods are goods that are both **excludable** (producers can prevent people who do not pay for them from using them) and **rivalrous** (one person’s use of the good reduces its availability to others).
 
• **Example**: Food, clothing, and personal gadgets.
 
• **Excludability**: Producers can prevent non-payers from accessing the goods.
 
• **Rivalry**: Consumption by one individual reduces the availability for others
 
 
 
• ​** Supplementary Goods**:
 
 
• These are goods that can be used as alternatives to other goods, meaning their consumption is related to or in place of another (e.g., tea and coffee as substitutes).
 
• **Alternatives**: Consumers may choose one good over the other based on price or preference.
 
• **Impact on Demand**: A price increase in one will generally increase demand for its substitute.
 
• **Example**: Tea and coffee, butter and margarine.

questions.question: In India, Micro Finance Institutions primarily target which segment of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Low-income individuals and small businesses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs)** are financial entities that provide small loans to people who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• In India, MFIs primarily target **low-income individuals** and **small businesses** to help them improve their livelihoods.
 
• These institutions aim to promote **financial inclusion** by providing credit to those who are underserved by formal financial institutions.
 
• MFIs often provide **loans** for purposes such as starting or expanding a small business, education, healthcare, and housing.
 
• By targeting low-income segments, MFIs help in **poverty alleviation** and economic development.

questions.question: The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the _____ Commission.

• The Indian Constitution's concept of five-year plans was influenced by the Soviet Union (now Russia), which had successfully implemented five-year plans for economic development.
 
• The Soviet system of economic planning had a particularly strong impact on Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• In order to direct its efforts at economic development after gaining independence, the Indian government created the concept of five-year plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was introduced in 1951, and the Planning Commission of India was founded to create and carry out these plans.
 
• The National Development Council (NDC) headed by the Prime Minister with all Chief Minister and cabinet ministers are the final authority to approve the five-year-long policy.
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formed India's Five-Year Plans.
 
 
 
• In 2014, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced to dissolve the Planning Commission and replace it by a new institution named NITI Aayog.

questions.question: The mixed economy is:

options.text: co-existence of traditional and modern industries
presence of domestic and foreign investments
a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention
presence of subsistence and commercial farming

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a socialist society the government decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with society's needs.
 
• In a **mixed economy**, the market will supply whatever goods and services it can produce well, and the government will provide essential goods and services that the market fails to do. 
 
• The mixed economic system is described as an economic system which combines the elements of a **planned economy** with those of a **market economy. **
 
• It is a mixture of capitalism and socialism, comprising both private and public corporations.
 
• A mixed economy structure is adopted by most developed economies.
 
• The elements of a capitalist economy and the elements of a command economy are synthesized into a mixed economic structure.
 
• Free economies co-exist with government interference in a mixed economic environment, and private businesses coexist with public enterprises.
 
• The benefits of a mixed economy include efficient production and capital distribution, as well as social security development.

questions.question: Which of the following does not come from sugarcane?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Honey:-**

 
 
• **It is a sweet, golden liquid produced by bees from the nectar of flowers.**
 
• It is a natural sweetener that has been used by humans for centuries.
 
• Honey is also a good source of antioxidants and other nutrients.
 
• **Honey does not come from sugarcane.**
 
• **Honey is produced by bees from the nectar of flowers. **

• **Sugar:-**

 
 
• **It is a refined product made from sugarcane juice. **
 
• The juice is boiled and crystallized, and the molasses is removed.
 
• Sugar is the most processed of the three products, and it is also the sweetest.
 
 
 
• **Khandsari:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of unrefined sugar that is made by boiling sugarcane juice until it thickens and forms crystals. **
 
• The molasses is not removed, so khandsari has a darker color and a more robust flavor than sugar.
 
 
 
• **Molasses:-**
 
 
• **It is a thick, dark syrup that is produced as a byproduct of sugar refining. **
 
• It contains the minerals and vitamins that are removed from sugar during processing.
 
• Molasses has a rich, sweet flavor and is often used in baking and cooking.

questions.question: Duties levied on goods produced within the country are ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**excise taxes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excise taxes:-**

 
 
• These are levied on goods produced within the country for domestic consumption.
 
• These taxes are imposed at the manufacturing stage and are included in the price of the product.
 
• Excise taxes are different from customs duties which are levied on goods imported into the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-dumping taxes:-**

 
 
• These are imposed on imported goods that are sold at prices lower than their normal value in the exporting country to protect the domestic industry. 
 
 
 
• **Wealth taxes:-**
 
 
• These are levied on the net wealth of individuals or companies and are not related to the production or sale of goods
 
 
 
• **Custom duties:-**
 
 
• These are taxes imposed on goods that are imported into the country from foreign nations. They are also known as import duties or tariffs.

questions.question: Which of these is a component of the tertiary sector of an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hotels and restaurants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __ Key Points__

__
 
• **Hotels and restaurants** are a component of the** tertiary sector **of an economy.
 
• The tertiary sector is also known as the **service sector, **and it includes all activities that provide services to** consumers **and other businesses.
 
• In the** three-sector model**, the third economic sector is the** tertiary sector.**
 
• The** primary** and** secondary** sectors are the others. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mining and quarrying** is a component of the **primary sector** of an economy, which includes all activities related to natural resources extraction.
 
• **Water supply** is a component of the **utility sector** of an economy, which includes all activities related to the provision of public utilities such as water, electricity, and gas.
 
• **Electricity** is also a component of the **utility sector** of an economy, as it is a public utility that is essential for many other economic activities.
 
• All operations with the ultimate goal of using up natural resources—**agricultural, fishing, forestry, mining, and deposits**—are included in the **primary sector.**
 
• The portion of the economy centered on manufacturing is known as the** secondary sector.**
 
 
• **Construction, fabrication, assembly, distillation, and purification** are examples of secondary sector activities.
